editorial:
Imagine spending your whole life being the only bridge between your mother and the world. That is exactly how Akito feels. His mom, Reiko, is deaf, and she has put all her hopes on him becoming a famous pianist. You can really feel the pressure he is under as he tries to get into a top music school while wondering if he is even good enough. The vibe is very emotional and sweet, especially when he meets Izumi. She is a deaf girl who plays music on the street and has a way of looking at life that makes Akito question everything his mother taught him. It is a touching story about family, expectations, and finding your own voice.

What really works here is the acting; you can feel the tension between the mother and son without them even speaking. The pacing is a bit slow, but it gives you time to care about the characters. If you like stories that make you cry and think about your parents, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday when you want something heartfelt.
endingExplained: At the end, Akito discovers that his mother actually struggled with her own dreams and regrets, which is why she pushed him so hard. He realizes her strictness came from a place of love and fear. He decides to stop playing just to please her and starts playing for himself. He reconciles with Reiko and accepts Izumi into his life, finding a balance between his music and his relationships.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching family dramas and stories about overcoming pressure.
